record.paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
record.original_question: What physical process produces the prompt high-energy emission in gamma-ray bursts, specifically what mechanism generates its nonthermal component, and does the prompt-emission spectrum also contain a photospheric thermal component? The unresolved alternatives named in the source are synchrotron radiation, jitter radiation, and synchrotron self-Compton emission for the nonthermal part, together with the separate possibility that thermal photospheric emission is present in the same prompt signal.

evidence.quote: It is noteworthy that the origin of the prompt high-energy emission is still being debated: What is the origin of the nonthermal component (synchrotron? jitter radiation? synchrotron self-Compton?), and is there also a photospheric thermal component present?

artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and observational studies through 2025–2026 (e.g., spectro-polarimetric analysis of GRB 230307A, modeling of radiation-mediated shocks, and the MDPI review "The GRB Prompt Emission: An Unsolved Puzzle") continue to debate whether the nonthermal component arises from synchrotron, jitter, or SSC emission, and whether a photospheric thermal component is generally present. Evidence supports hybrid models with transitions between photospheric- and synchrotron-dominated phases, but no consensus mechanism has been established. The problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: The GRB Prompt Emission: An Unsolved Puzzle

status_evidence.claim: The radiative mechanism of GRB prompt emission is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Time-resolved spectro-polarimetric analysis of GRB 230307A
status_evidence.snippet: Possible evidence of evolution from photospheric to synchrotron dominated emission.
status_evidence.claim: Both photospheric thermal and nonthermal synchrotron components may contribute, with transitions between regimes; the dominant mechanism is still under investigation.

status_evidence.title: GRB prompt emission from synchrotron radiation in a rapidly decaying magnetic field
status_evidence.snippet: Modeling synchrotron emission with decaying magnetic fields as a candidate mechanism.
status_evidence.claim: Synchrotron with decaying fields is still an actively pursued candidate, indicating no settled answer.
